findings.body: The doc contract says "Shorten `text` to at most `limit` characters", but when `head` contains no space the `None` branch returns `head` (exactly `limit` chars) plus the `…` ellipsis (1 char), i.e. `limit + 1` characters. The caller is described as check-run titles under GitHub's character ceiling, so a title with no space in the first `limit` chars (a URL, a long identifier, a path) produces output that exceeds the limit the function promises to enforce. Reserve one character for the ellipsis up front so both branches stay within `limit`.
findings.title: Reserve room for the ellipsis in shorten's no-space branch

value.summary: The module adds `shorten` and `first_sentence` helpers with correct char-boundary handling and tests. One correctness issue: `shorten` can return `limit + 1` characters on input with no space in the first `limit` chars, violating its own documented ceiling — relevant since it targets GitHub's check-run title limit.
